conventions.ps: Metric horsepower (PS) as badged/quoted in the UK; null where not confirmed.
conventions.engine_code: Manufacturer engine code where well established; null where not confident.
conventions.status: verified = core trims and main powertrains corroborated by UK sources found during research (finer details may still be general knowledge, see notes); general-knowledge = compiled from established knowledge without direct source confirmation in this pass.
conventions.derivative_pattern: Make Model Generation Badge Trim Doors Transmission, e.g. 'Nissan Juke F15 1.6 Acenta 5dr Xtronic CVT'

models.notes: Launch Jan 2014 with 1.2 DIG-T as only petrol; 1.6 DIG-T added later in 2014 (one source quotes 150PS; UK spec widely quoted 163PS, manual only). Xtronic CVT on 1.2 DIG-T and 1.6 dCi; 1.6 dCi 130 offered with 4WD (ALL-MODE 4x4-i). 1.3 DIG-T 160 available with 7-speed DCT from late 2018; 1.5 dCi 115 DCT also offered. Special editions: Bose Personal Edition, N-Motion. Also Qashqai+2 not in this generation.

MHEV 140 manual only; MHEV 158 manual or Xtronic, 4WD (ALL-MODE 4x4-i) with Xtronic on upper trims. e-Power: 1.5 VC-Turbo 3-cyl petrol generator, wheels driven by electric motor only (approx 190PS / some UK sources 187bhp; Autocar quotes 203bhp - treat as unconfirmed). Upgraded third-generation e-Power announced 2025 - output not confirmed here. No diesel.

1.6 94PS = 5-speed manual only; 1.6 117PS (some data 112-119PS) = Xtronic CVT. 1.6 DIG-T 190: 6-speed manual FWD or Xtronic CVT with ALL-MODE 4x4-i. Nismo RS 218PS FWD manual; 4WD CVT version 214PS. 1.5 dCi 6-speed manual (5-speed pre-facelift) FWD only. Nismo trims/outputs vary by source (Nismo RS 214-218PS).

1.0 DIG-T 3-cyl turbo, manual or DCT. Hybrid (from 2022): 1.6 petrol + electric motor + multi-mode dog-clutch auto (4 engine speeds, 2 motor speeds); offered Acenta Premium upward, not Visia. Trim naming varies ('Tekna+' vs 'Tekna Plus').

Hybrid (from mid-2012) e-CVT only, 5dr only. 1.33 available with 6-speed manual or Multidrive S CVT; 1.0 5-speed manual. 1.5 2NR-FKE replaced the 1.33 at 2017 facelift; diesel dropped c.2017. Excel became hybrid-only after 2017. GRMN 3dr limited run (UK c.2018). Trim names pre-2014 from general knowledge.

UK Yaris hatch is hybrid-only (1.5 petrol non-hybrid sold in some EU markets, not standard UK). From 2024 Icon/Design keep 116PS, Excel/GR Sport get 130PS. GR Yaris is the 3dr homologation model (Circuit Pack trim); Yaris Cross is a separate model not covered here. Dynamic trim existed early (2020-22) - general knowledge.

1.2T petrol dropped Dec 2019; range hybrid-only thereafter. Saloon 1.8 hybrid only. 2.0 hybrid listed by Toyota UK price lists as '2.0 VVT-i 178 DIN hp' (pre-2023 sources quote 180 or 184PS). 2023 update: 5th-gen hybrid, 140PS/196PS. Trek trim Touring Sports only.
1.2T: 6-speed manual FWD or CVT AWD (AWD dropped early). Hybrid e-CVT FWD only. 2.0 hybrid added at 2019/2020 facelift. Toyota's 2.0 often quoted 184PS (some UK sources 178 DIN hp).

1.8 on Icon/Design/Excel; 2.0 on GR Sport and Premiere Edition (AWD-i option on 2.0). PHEV (Toyota UK '223 DIN hp'; some sources 226PS) on Design, Excel, GR Sport. Some sources quote 2.0 HEV as 196/197PS.

KX- prefix denoted AWD pre-facelift; dropped at 2018 facelift (AWD badge instead). Facelift: 1.7 CRDi replaced by 1.6 CRDi (115/136, 7DCT available); 2.0 CRDi 185 became 48V 'EcoDynamics+' mild hybrid with 8-speed auto. 1.6 T-GDi 6MT or 7DCT. Sources conflict on whether 48V MHEV applied to 1.6 or 2.0 diesel in UK (both reported). Trims-by-engine matrix not verified.

Facelift (2025) drops mild-hybrid; entry is 1.6 T-GDi ICE ~149PS manual/DCT. Facelift HEV quoted 238-239PS (Honest John 238PS; Kia UK 207bhp on one page - conflicting), PHEV uplifted (one source 283bhp) - left null. Diesel was UK-launch only and not offered post-facelift. Pre-facelift trim list ('4' and 'Black Edition') from general knowledge. Engine codes G4FP/G4FT = Smartstream 1.6 T-GDi (general knowledge).

ProCeed (GT-Line, GT-Line S, GT only) and Sportswagon share platform; PHEV was Sportswagon only (UK). XCeed is a separate model. 1.5 T-GDi appears at 138bhp (140PS) and 158bhp (160PS) in What Car? listings. UK sales ended 2025. Codes G3LC/G4LD/G4LH/G4FJ/D4FE/G4LE general knowledge.

Mechanically twinned with Kia Sportage QL. Facelift 2018: 1.7 CRDi replaced by 1.6 CRDi; 2.0 CRDi 185 became 48V mild hybrid with 8-speed auto; N Line added 2019. Trim list confirmed only partially (VehicleScore lists S Blue Drive, SE Nav, Premium SE, N Line, Ultimate); engine list general knowledge.

UK range all 1.6 T-GDi Smartstream; no diesel in UK. Facelift HEV/PHEV outputs revised (Europe c.215PS HEV / 252PS PHEV reported - not confirmed for UK, left null). 2026 trim reshuffle per Hyundai UK press release.

Launch: SE Connect, Premium, Ultimate (Hyundai UK press kit); N Line and i20 N (6MT only) added 2021. Post-2023 facelift trim names and non-MHEV 1.0 T-GDi from general knowledge. G3LE code general knowledge. i20 N ended 2024.

PureTech 75 5MT; PureTech 100 6MT (EAT8 option pre-facelift); PureTech 130 EAT8 (GT). Facelift (UK orders late 2023/2024) adds 48V Hybrid 100/136 with e-DCS6 (later rebadged 110/145 in some markets - not confirmed UK). Engine codes general knowledge. Mid-cycle trim names (Premium variants) partly general knowledge; facelift trims verified.

2023 facelift: PureTech 100 Active-only 6MT; PureTech 130 Allure/GT 6MT or EAT8. PureTech 155 EAT8 GT only. BlueHDi 110 6MT, BlueHDi 130 EAT8. Hybrid 136/145 confirmed by Auto Express listings (GT, Envy). Engine codes general knowledge (EB2ADTX for 155 not certain).

EAT6 used 2016-2018, replaced by EAT8. 2.0 BlueHDi 180 GT auto only. Plug-in hybrids from early 2020. Hybrid 136 MHEV appeared in final months before E-3008 (Mk3, 2024) replaced it. GT Line reportedly discontinued end-2021. Engine codes and early trim mapping general knowledge; THP 165 and 2.0 BlueHDi not confirmed by search results.

Launched March 2013 with 1.2/1.4 TSI, 1.6/2.0 TDI; Elegance renamed SE L. vRS from mid-2013 (petrol/diesel, estate too); vRS 245 from 2017 facelift; 4x4 vRS TDI. Scout estate AWD only (2.0 TDI 150/184, 1.8 TSI). Power outputs by year approximate - general knowledge. Engine codes deliberately left null.

e-TEC = 48V mild hybrid, DSG only. iV PHEV uses 6-speed DSG (SE L iV 204, vRS iV 245); PHEV dropped with 2024 facelift. Facelift (UK from 2024) replaces 1.0 TSI with 1.5 TSI 115 on SE Technology; vRS 265PS petrol only (vRS diesel dropped in UK - general knowledge). Carwow lists 1.5 petrol at 116/150bhp and 2.0 TDI at 116/150bhp post-facelift.

2014-2019: JCW (with Pepper, Chili, Media options packs)

models.notes: Picker derivative is typically engine variant + trim, e.g. 'MINI Hatch F56 Cooper Sport 3dr Steptronic'. Classic/Sport/Exclusive introduced 2019 (One = Classic only from 2021). Cooper S output reduced to 178PS with WLTP/2021 facelift (sources 176-178bhp). F57 Convertible not included. Diesels dropped c.2020. Engine codes general knowledge; Cooper S 192 vs 178 timing approximate.

Tesla does not publish official PS figures for most variants - left null. Variant is the trim; battery packs vary by build (LFP in SR+/RWD from c.2021). Highland facelift deliveries UK from late 2023; Performance Highland 2024. Long Range RWD availability in UK general knowledge.

UK RHD deliveries from 2022. Juniper launch: Launch Series LR AWD £60,990, wider range from c.April-June 2025 from £44,990. No 7-seat in UK post-facelift. PS figures not published - null. Standard and Long Range RWD UK availability partly general knowledge.

Launch prices (UK 2019): D150 FWD manual, D150/D180/D240/P200/P250/P300 AWD auto. MY21 Ingenium diesel update replaced D150/D180/D240 with D165/D200 (outputs ~163/204PS). P300e: 1.5 3-cyl + rear e-motor, 8-speed auto. Facelift (MY24, mid-2023) simplified trims. D165/D200/P300e engine codes not confirmed. Ingenium codes general knowledge. P160 3-cyl (FWD) existed in some markets - UK availability uncertain.
